changelog.reason: Initial record (single read, unattended research run) from uphold.com US and UK card pages, the US Card Rewards terms (last updated 2 Nov 2026) and two support articles (rewards programme; ordering/limits/fees). Two contradictions recorded (Essential reward 1 % vs 2 %; Essential foreign transaction 1.50 % vs $1.50 flat). KYC steps and top-up costs unknown. US rewards are offered 'for a limited time' with no end date.

editorial.summary: Uphold's debit card spends directly from the Uphold account. In the US (Visa, Cross River Bank) the free Essential card pays 1 % in XRP (cap $120/month) and the $99.99/year Elite card 3–4 % in XRP (cap $300/month) with no FX or ATM fee; in the UK (Mastercard, Optimus Cards) a free card pays 1 % GBP cashback on cash-funded purchases (cap £100/month). The US rewards are offered 'for a limited time' without an end date.
good_for: US residents (outside LA/NY) who hold XRP or other assets at Uphold and want rewards paid in XRP
UK Uphold users wanting a free card with modest GBP cashback on cash spending
not_for: Residents outside the US and the UK (EEA availability not stated)
UK users who want cashback on crypto-funded purchases (excluded)
Anyone needing a confirmed long-term reward rate: the US programme is 'for a limited time' and the product page caps the reward value at 3 months after activation
watch_outs: Essential card reward: 1 % per the dated terms and product page, 2 % per a support article — the lower figure is modelled.
Essential foreign transaction fee: 1.50 % (product page) vs $1.50 flat (support article).
'Rewards Currency' is any crypto Uphold chooses ('currently XRP'); reward value converts at Uphold's rate on disbursement.
Spending crypto from the card is a taxable disposal (stated by Uphold); UK cashback is only earned on GBP-funded purchases.
Identity-verification steps and top-up/trading costs are not stated on the pages read — unknown, not free.
